ordered_diagnoses: Acquired Cutaneous Amyloidosis (Secondary to Multiple Myeloma)

s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive painful skin lesions and ulcers with systemic symptoms and multiple myeloma history
salient_findings: Progressive painful blisters and ulcers of the groin
Enlargement of the tongue with difficulty in mastication
Numbness of distal lower limbs without weakness
Circinate purpuric patches with erosions on the skin
Macroglossia, glossitis, and hemorrhagic erosion on the hard palate
key_facts: 1-week history of progressive painful blisters and ulcers
3-month history of tongue enlargement
3-month history of numbness in distal lower limbs
History of IgG λ-type multiple myeloma
Anemia and lytic lesions in the calvarium
Taking folic acid and intramuscular cyanocobalamin supplements
Platelet count within reference range
Low serum zinc level
Subepidermal blister with chronic inflammatory infiltrate on biopsy
Eosinophilic bands in the dermis with apple-green birefringence on polarized light microscopy
Negative direct immunofluorescence test
Negative Herpes simplex virus PCR from perineal ulcer swab

shortlist: Acquired Cutaneous Amyloidosis (Secondary to Multiple Myeloma)

shortlist.label: Multiple myeloma-associated amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: History of IgG λ-type multiple myeloma and biopsy findings of subepidermal blister with chronic inflammatory infiltrate and eosinophilic bands in the dermis showing apple-green birefringence on polarized light microscopy

shortlist.label: AL (primary) amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Biopsy findings of subepidermal blister with chronic inflammatory infiltrate and eosinophilic bands in the dermis showing apple-green birefringence on polarized light microscopy

shortlist.label: Systemic amyloidosis (AL type)
shortlist.why_kept: History of IgG λ-type multiple myeloma and biopsy findings of subepidermal blister with chronic inflammatory infiltrate and eosinophilic bands in the dermis showing apple-green birefringence on polarized light microscopy

shortlist.label: Bullous amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Biopsy findings of subepidermal blister with chronic inflammatory infiltrate and eosinophilic bands in the dermis showing apple-green birefringence on polarized light microscopy

shortlist.label: Acquired Cutaneous Amyloidosis (Secondary to Multiple Myeloma)
shortlist.why_kept: History of IgG λ-type multiple myeloma and biopsy findings of subepidermal blister with chronic inflammatory infiltrate and eosinophilic bands in the dermis showing apple-green birefringence on polarized light microscopy

raw.rationale: The patient's history of IgG λ-type multiple myeloma and the presence of eosinophilic bands in the dermis with apple-green birefringence on polarized light microscopy, which is characteristic of amyloid deposits, support this diagnosis. The patient's symptoms, including progressive painful blisters and ulcers, tongue enlargement, and numbness in distal lower limbs, are also consistent with systemic amyloidosis.

rejected.label: Multiple myeloma-associated amyloidosis
rejected.why: While the patient has multiple myeloma, this option is too broad and does not specifically indicate the type of amyloidosis.

rejected.label: AL (primary) amyloidosis
rejected.why: This option is similar to the champion, but 'primary' is not necessary as the patient has a known plasma cell dyscrasia (multiple myeloma).

rejected.label: Bullous amyloidosis
rejected.why: This option is too narrow, focusing only on the cutaneous manifestations, and does not account for the patient's systemic symptoms.

rejected.label: Acquired Cutaneous Amyloidosis (Secondary to Multiple Myeloma)
rejected.why: This option is incorrect because the patient's amyloidosis is not limited to the skin and has systemic involvement.
